subject.title: fix(repair): publish only validated target commits

question: Should repair execution permanently require Linux delegated namespaces and Landlock ABI 3+ as a fail-closed contract, or should immutable publication be separated from that runner requirement?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and well-proven, but it deliberately trades compatibility and repair availability for a stronger credential-bearing execution boundary; automation cannot choose that permanent operational contract.

options.title: Accept contained Linux contract
options.body: Keep the integrated design, resolve the merge state, and require successful exact-head hosted proof before merge.

options.title: Split immutable publication
options.body: Land isolated exact-SHA Git publication separately while retaining the containment work for a narrower runner-contract review.

options.title: Pause for portable design
options.body: Keep the PR draft until maintainers define a supported non-Linux or lower-Landlock execution model.

recommendation.title: Accept contained Linux contract
recommendation.body: Keep the integrated design, resolve the merge state, and require successful exact-head hosted proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest available ownership signal for the exact repair security design and its proof suite.
